messages:
marie: Quick sync — we need a fallback parity matrix for tiered routing + region-aware fallbacks. EU enterprise customers require tool-calling parity and 32k+ context for some workflows. Who owns the matrix and where should it live?

sam: I can take point on a draft. Clarify scope: are we listing every variant we currently serve (hosted/dedicated/private) or just recommended fallbacks per route? :thinking:

devon: Prefer: per-route recommended fallback list + a separate column for absolute compatibility constraints. Tokenizer parity is the big one — some quantized builds change tokenization edge cases (split points). That breaks tool-calling signatures.

li: Proposed minimal schema (columns):
- variant_id
- tokenizer_match (yes/partial/no)
- ctx_max (e.g., 32k)
- toolcall_supported (yes/partial/no)
- kv_cache_compatible (yes/no)
- latency_delta_ms
- recommended_tiers (list)

Sample snippet for the matrix (first-pass):
```
variant_id,gpt-open-32k-q4
tokenizer_match,yes
ctx_max,32768
toolcall_supported,yes
kv_cache_compatible,yes
latency_delta_ms,+18
recommended_tiers,enterprise,dedicated
---
variant_id,gpt-open-8k-q2
tokenizer_match,partial
ctx_max,8192
toolcall_supported,partial
kv_cache_compatible,no
latency_delta_ms,-5
recommended_tiers,hosted,burst
```

ashok: UX note — Console needs a per-route "Fallback policy" panel (toggle allow/deny, list of allowed fallback variants, hard-fail if toolcall parity required). Show an inline badge when a request is served from fallback with reason: capacity/region/ctx-overflow. :eyes:

sam: Telemetry we should emit on every fallback: `fallback.triggered`, `fallback.reason`, `fallback.from_variant`, `fallback.to_variant`, `fallback.truncated_tokens`. These should be in the route-level billing/usage events so we can correlate SLA/tier billing differences.

devon: Runtime check needs to be deterministic and fast: before routing choose candidate variant, run a small compatibility check: tokenizer equivalence on prefix tokens + toolcall signature check (if request contains function calls). If incompatible, either skip variant or mark as "partial" and run with a degrade path that strips tool calls and warn.

li: Storage/location options: keep canonical matrix as a versioned JSON in infra-config repo and expose via config API (`/v1/fallback-matrix?v=2`). That way dedicated/private can pin to config version. Example config blob (very small):
```
{version:2,variants:[{id:gpt-open-32k-q4,tokenizer_match:yes,...}]}
```
(no need for full schema here, just example)

ashok: Billing question: if a user requests 32k model but we fallback to 8k with equivalent output (unlikely), do we bill at requested model rate or served model rate? My vote: bill at served model rate and add an event to inform the customer in console and via webhook. For SLAs we can make exceptions on enterprise contracts.

sam: Agreed on served-rate billing by default. We should include a flag in route config `preserve_billing_on_fallback:true` for special customers.

marie: Action items — Sam: draft initial matrix and push to infra-config repo. Li: draft JSON schema and API shape. Ashok: mock console UI and fallback banner copy. Devon: implement runtime quick-check prototype and list known tokenizer edgecases. I'll consolidate and schedule a 30m review next Tue.

infra-bot: Deploy check — created issue infra/config#412: "fallback-matrix v2 schema + API" (assigned to sam).

sam: thanks — starting PR today. If anyone has test prompts that exercise toolcall+ctx boundaries, paste them in this thread.

marie: will add a few customer repros (EU-telemetry and a docs webhook case). :thumbsup:
